findings.F1: The tested idea's gain sits almost entirely in the largest clearances. Closes more than 1.5 units of 20-day volatility above the prior 20-day high were followed by +11.9 % excess over 10 days (t 2.73, 94 cases), and by +11.2 % when coins are averaged per date first (t 2.01, 47 dates, 74 % of coins positive). Clearances of 0 to 0.5 units were followed by +0.3 % (t 0.19, 127 cases) and of 0.5 to 1.5 units by +1.4 % (t 1.15, 151 cases).
findings.F2: The large-clearance move builds up through the 10-day horizon but does not reach 20 days. The excess after clearances above 1.5 units is +2.3 % over 3 days (date-clustered t 2.44, 126 cases), +5.0 % over 5 days (t 1.60, 81), +11.2 % over 10 days (t 2.01, 47) and +5.7 % over 20 days (t 0.91, 24). The 20-day figure is too thin to show a giveback.
findings.F3: Within breakouts, a positive 60-day return went with a larger continuation, but the trend measure did not grade it. The 10-day excess was +5.4 % after a positive 60-day return (t 2.35, 187 cases) and +2.0 % after a negative one (t 1.36, 185 cases). Strong clearances in a rising 60 days gave +10.7 % against +3.5 % in a falling one. By 60-day terciles, averaged per date, the order was not monotone: +7.0 %, +4.1 % and +4.6 %, with t 0.67 to 1.70.
findings.F4: Thursday shows a 10-day excess of +4.3 % pooled (t 3.98, 484 cases), positive for 18 of 19 coins and in all 8 years. Averaged per date it drops to t 0.96 over only 43 dates, so it is a handful of shared dates, not a weekday effect.
findings.F5: The other angles showed nothing graded or robust. The middle volatility quartile gave −2.7 % (t −3.97), but the quartiles on either side were positive, so there is no gradient. Falls of 1 to 2 volatility units on the last day gave +2.6 % (t 2.96), next to −0.1 % to −1.5 % for the neighbouring bins. The deepest closes below the 20-day low gave +2.2 % (t 1.63). The 60-day return quintiles over 20 days gave t from −2.42 to +0.64, not monotone.
findings.F6: The years split the excess between strongly positive and strongly negative. It was −4.7 % in 2018 (t −3.61), −3.8 % in 2022 (t −5.66) and −2.0 % in 2025 (t −3.42), against +2.0 % to +4.0 % in 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024. That is moves the coins share, not a pattern of one coin's own bars.
findings.F7: The book's best 2 % of days (739 coin-days) came with a coin return of +12.4 % after a 5-day run of +24.1 %. Its worst 2 % came with a coin return of −8.6 % after a flat 5 days (+0.6 %). The book earns on strong running breakouts and loses on sudden falls from quiet stretches, consistent with the tested idea.

no_ideas: Across about fifteen angles (clearance, breakdown below the low, last-day and 3-day moves, 60-day trend, volatility level, weekday, year, horizons of 3 to 20 days, and the book's tails), the only pattern that stands out is the tested idea's own large-clearance continuation (F1, F2), and the rest is either ungraded (F3, F5) or disappears once coins are averaged per date (F4, F6), so no new idea is supported.
